correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=3, a generic centroidal hyperplane intersects exactly the simplex edges joining normal coordinates with opposite signs. If K is the number of positive coordinates, N_m=K(m-K)=m²/4-(K-m/2)². A Haar normal on the zero-sum space is the direction of Y_i=Z_i-mean(Z), iid Z_i~N(0,1). Its off-diagonal correlation is -1/(m-1), so the bivariate Gaussian opposite-sign probability is arccos[-1/(m-1)]/pi and summing over C(m,2) edges yields the stated mean exactly. Expanding arcsin at 1/(m-1) yields m²/4-sigma² m+O(1/m), sigma²=1/4-1/(2pi). The source grid/Chebyshev argument correctly establishes empirical-CDF stochastic equicontinuity at the random sample mean; the independent influence representation is m^-1/2 sum [1{Z_i>0}-1/2-phi(0)Z_i]+o_p(1), with variance sigma². The iid CLT, continuous mapping and Slutsky give the two asserted chi-square limits. m=3 gives N_3=2 deterministically and the exact formula agrees. Independent Gaussian simulation m=3,4,8,32,256,1000 agreed with expectation within sample fluctuation and normalized K variance approached sigma²; finite data are corroboration only, not proof of limit. All normalization, quantifiers, genericity and boundary cases checked.

value.rationale: A Haar-random central simplex section vertex count is intrinsically natural, and its exact expectation and chi-square scaling are meaningful invariants. It is an instructive specialization but not an independent valuable research contribution under the shared C/O/V standard.
